title: Vowels Game in a String
summary: Alice and Bob play a game on a string.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game on a string. Alice starts. On her turn, Alice removes a non-empty substring with an odd number of vowels. On Bob's turn, he removes a non-empty substring with an even number of vowels. The player who can't make a move loses. Return true if Alice wins, false otherwise. The vowels are a, e, i, o, and u.
constraints: Alice removes a nonempty substring with an odd vowel count.
Bob removes one with an even vowel count; a player without a move loses.
Return whether Alice wins with optimal play.
reference_solution:
def alice_wins_vowel_game(s):
    return any(c in 'aeiou' for c in s)
hints: Alice has a legal first move exactly when at least one vowel exists.
If a vowel exists, game parity lets Alice remove an odd-vowel segment and answer Bob’s even-vowel removals.
Test whether any character is in the vowel set.
With no vowel Alice loses immediately; with one she has the standard winning strategy.
editorial: With no vowel Alice loses immediately; with one she has the standard winning strategy.

tests.explanation: The string contains vowels, allowing Alice to force a win.
Alice has no substring with an odd vowel count and loses immediately.
